mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with reduced discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is continuous and negative: lower rates predict higher returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 225.0, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The threshold is set at 225.0 based on the current value of 224.304.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 225.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 8.0%) and weak employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% monthly) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The interaction of these two series is the signal.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (UNRATE > 8.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.5%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, defined by a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.5% over the past 6 months, leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. This reflects market concerns about reduced liquidity and economic growth.
failure_condition: The signal (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% in 6 months) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic activity and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is continuous and positive: higher INDPRO predicts higher returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high INDPRO periods (INDPRO > 95.0) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600.0 and residential sales (RSAFS) fall below 390000.0, the housing demand slowdown signals negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The interaction of these two series is the signal.
failure_condition: HOUST < 600.0 AND RSAFS < 390000.0 and returns are positive in more than 40% of such instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The relationship is continuous and positive: higher GDP growth predicts higher equity returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in high GDP growth periods (GDPC1 > 13300.0) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The current low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS = 0.07%) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting immediate market sentiment towards accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
